subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for August 01, 2026.
Today we will review 2 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 1 - Safety and outcomes of dapagliflozin initiation in critically
sentences: Story 1 is about Safety and outcomes of dapagliflozin initiation in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury: A post-hoc analysis of the defender trial..
This is a recent research article from Journal of critical care.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in patients with AKI at enrollment (100 dapagliflozin, 112 control), we compared 28-day mortality, kidney replacement therapy (KRT), and composite death/KRT, how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
Event rates were similar: 28-day mortality 38% vs 40%, KRT 12% vs 18%, composite 41% vs 42% (dapagliflozin vs control).
Adjusted risk differences were - 1.9% (95% CI -14.5 to 10.7) for death, -7.4% (-16.2 to 1.5) for KRT, and - 0.9% (-13.6 to 11.8) for the composite.
Physiological trajectories showed no divergence suggestive of hemodynamic or metabolic instability.
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use as an awareness item; read the full article before applying it clinically.

script.heading: Story 2 - Dose-response association between intraoperative norepinephrin
sentences: Story 2 is about Dose-response association between intraoperative norepinephrine and postoperative acute kidney injury: a retrospective cohort study..
This is a cohort study from British journal of anaesthesia.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in Critically ill or ICU-relevant patients described in the abstract; confirm eligibility criteria in the full text., how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
Norepinephrine was administered in 1232 patients (4.4%), and AKI occurred in 4448 (16.0%).

Restricted cubic spline analyses showed significant nonlinearity for unit-rate metrics (maximum dose P=0.008; time-weighted intensity P=0.022), whereas time-integrated metrics were linear (AUC P=0.10; duration P=0.50).
Dose-duration (P=0.286) and dose-hypotension interactions (P=0.298) were non-significant, supporting additive effects.
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use as background evidence; look for confounding and whether the exposure is modifiable at the bedside.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Outro
sentences: That wraps up today's journal club style update.
Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.
For English practice, repeat one academic phrase from each article out loud.

articles.title: Dose-response association between intraoperative norepinephrine and postoperative acute kidney injury: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.summary: Norepinephrine was administered in 1232 patients (4.4%), and AKI occurred in 4448 (16.0%). Restricted cubic spline analyses showed significant nonlinearity for unit-rate metrics (maximum dose P=0.008; time-weighted intensity P=0.022), whereas time-integrated metrics were linear (AUC P=0.10; duration P=0.50). Dose-duration (P=0.286) and dose-hypotension interactions (P=0.298) were non-significant, supporting additive effects. A maximum norepinephrine dose of >0.029 μg kg-1 min-1 remained independently associated with AKI (odds ratio [OR] 1.76; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.41-2.20; P<0.001); adjustment for intraoperative hypotension minimally attenuated this association (5.1%; adjusted OR 1.71; 95% CI 1.36-2.15). Intraoperative norepinephrine is associated with postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI), but bedside-readable dose anchors remain undefined.
